story.iWant: I want to build the high-effort custom components defined in the UX specification,
story.soThat: So that the core user workflows are intuitive and engaging.
story.tasks: - [ ] Task 1: Implement Document Preview Component (AC: #1) - [ ] Create the basic structure for the component. - [ ] Implement states: default, loading, error. - [ ] Implement actions: view, delete, generate summary/quiz. - [ ] Task 2: Implement Drag-and-Drop Upload Area (AC: #2) - [ ] Create the UI for the dropzone. - [ ] Add file type and size validation. - [ ] Implement drag-and-drop functionality using a library like `react-dropzone`. - [ ] Ensure full accessibility (keyboard navigation, screen reader support). - [ ] Task 3: Implement Loading Screen/Modal for Generation (AC: #3) - [ ] Design a reusable modal component. - [ ] Display progress information (e.g., "Analyzing document...", "Generating summary..."). - [ ] Integrate with the summary/quiz generation workflows. - [ ] Task 4: Implement Quiz Interface (AC: #4) - [ ] Create the component to display questions and multiple-choice answers. - [ ] Implement logic to handle answer selection and feedback. - [ ] Style the component according to the UX design. - [ ] Task 5: Implement Summary View Component (AC: #4) - [ ] Create the component to display the generated summary text. - [ ] Add actions like "Copy to Clipboard" or "Save". - [ ] Style the component according to the UX design. - [ ] Task 6: Testing - [ ] Write unit tests for each custom component. - [ ] Write integration tests to ensure components work together correctly. - [ ] Manually test all components for functionality, accessibility, and adherence to UX specifications.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** the core UI foundation is in place, **when** the custom components are built, **then** the `Document Preview Component` is implemented with all its specified states and actions. 2. **And** the `Drag-and-Drop Upload Area` is fully functional and accessible. 3. **And** the `Loading Screen/Modal for Generation` provides clear user feedback. 4. **And** the `Quiz Interface` and `Summary View` components are implemented as designed.

constraints.constraint: New custom components must be built as reusable React components.
All new custom components must be fully accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA) and responsive.
New components should be placed in a logical structure within the `src/components` directory, specifically `src/components/ui/`.
Adherence to existing project conventions for component organization and styling (Tailwind CSS) is required.

tests.standards: Unit tests for individual components using Jest. Integration tests for workflows. Manual End-to-End (E2E) testing for functionality, accessibility, and adherence to UX specifications.

ideas.idea: Unit tests for `Document Preview Component` covering default, loading, and error states, and all specified actions (view, delete, generate summary/quiz).
Unit tests for `Drag-and-Drop Upload Area` covering UI rendering, file type/size validation, and drag-and-drop functionality.
Accessibility tests for `Drag-and-Drop Upload Area` ensuring keyboard navigation and screen reader support.
Unit tests for `Loading Screen/Modal for Generation` covering progress information display and integration with content generation workflows.
Unit tests for `Quiz Interface` covering question display, multiple-choice answer selection, and feedback logic.
Unit tests for `Summary View Component` covering display of generated summary text and actions like "Copy to Clipboard" or "Save".
Integration tests to ensure that the custom UX components work correctly together within the core user workflows.
Manual E2E testing for all custom components to verify functionality, accessibility, and visual adherence to UX specifications.
